text:
samira.k: Hi team — accepted the GitHub invite but get a 400 error that says 'invite cannot be accepted: email alias detected'. I used samira.k@redwood.ai, which forwards to samira+kitchen@redwood.ai due to my inbox rules. Anyone seen this?
ryan-peopleops: welcome Samira! Tagging IT: @it-bot — forwarding rules can cause delivery normalization. Can you paste the exact error screenshot or copy the message?
samira.k: it shows: 'Invite rejected: email alias not allowed. Contact org admin.' The invite link is the one in the welcome email.
it-bot: Thanks — checking org logs. Quick explanation: our org policy disallows plus-addressing and forwarding during account creation because GitHub normalizes and sometimes attaches to an existing account. Two clean options: (1) Accept on a browser/session where your work address is the active GitHub user (incognito if needed), or (2) we issue a 'create-new-account' invite that forces a fresh account on that email. Which do you prefer?
samira.k: I'd like a fresh work account separate from my personal GH. Also need immediate read access to redwood/docs and onboarding repo.
eli-eng: if you need to start work ASAP, I can temporarily add you as a collaborator on a single repo while IT sorts the org invite. But prefer org teams for audit.
it-bot: Reissuing as create-new-account at 2026-09-11T13:02:05Z and pre-adding to docs-readers + onboarding. Note: our org requires 2FA and SAML SSO. Please have your Okta invite completed before accepting or SSO may block.
devex-jo: Quick tip: Accept the invite, then run `gh auth login --web` to map the local gh client to the new account — avoids VSCode token mixups.
samira.k: Accepted the new invite but when I create the account, the flow says 'SSO provisioning pending' and I get a 403 on private repos.
it-bot: That means Okta hasn't provisioned your SSO status yet. Can you confirm you completed Okta enrollment? Check for an Okta invite email or go to our IdP portal.
samira.k: I did enroll, but my Okta profile shows groups: 'engineering' only. The provisioning mapping expects 'engineering-dev' for repo access.
ryan-peopleops: @samira.k — I can add you to the correct Okta group. One sec.
it-bot: Manual SCIM sync requested at 2026-09-11T13:14:40Z. After SCIM completes, GitHub should mark SSO approved and teams will appear within a minute or two.
samira.k: SCIM finished and SSO is approved. I can see the org teams now, but `git clone git@github.com:redwood/docs.git` returns "Permission denied (publickey)".
eli-eng: Sounds like SSH key mismatch — did you add the work SSH public key to the work GitHub account? Sometimes people add the key to personal account accidentally.
samira.k: I uploaded a key but maybe uploaded the wrong one. How do I check which key the ssh-agent is offering?
devex-jo: Run `ssh -T git@github.com -vvv` and look for the identity files offered. If it's offering a personal key, either run `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa_work` or edit `~/.ssh/config` to point github.com to your work key.
samira.k: Fixed ssh-agent and can clone now. One more: I opened infra/repo-access for write to redwood/docs for a small PR. How do approvals usually work?
eli-eng: infra/repo-access requests are reviewed by infra team; small doc PRs usually get approved same-day. Tag me on the request if it's urgent.
it-bot: FYI for future hires: if you keep mail forwarding or plus-addressing enabled, we recommend temporarily disabling it while accepting invites to avoid alias normalization issues. Also prefer accepting invites in a clean browser session tied to the intended account.
samira.k: All good now — can push to my fork and opened the access request. Thanks for the quick help everyone! :tada:
